chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah ibn Mihran said:

I asked him about a man who had a wife and then married another woman over her, is it permissible for him to favor one over the other? He said: He should favor the newlywed for the three days of her wedding celebration, if she is a virgin. Then he should equalize between them with the goodwill of one of them towards the other.

key_terms.حِدثَانَ عُرسِهَا: the days of her wedding celebration

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on favoring one wife over another in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Samaan ibn Mihran, clarifying that the 'preference' (faddl) granted to a new virgin bride for three days refers to temporary exclusive companionship or favor in intimacy, rather than unequal division of time or wealth. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence to ensure that the mandatory equalization (qist) between wives is maintained in all other aspects after this brief period of special attention.
